text:
sam: FYI - ran a focused eval this morning on the new quantized encoder (harbor-int4) for array-style funcalls. Seeing a curious failure mode: arrays in params occasionally arrive with elements permuted or with a missing index (e.g., [a,b,c] -> [a,c] or [b,a,c]). Consumer-facing failure ~0.18% in staging.
rachel: whoa. arrays getting reordered? paste raw examples please.
sam: snippets from logs:
```
{"tool":"bulk_update","params":{"ids":[101,102,103],"flags":["x","y","z"]}}
{"tool":"bulk_update","params":{"ids":[101,103],"flags":["x","z"]}}
{"tool":"bulk_update","params":{"ids":[102,101,103],"flags":["y","x","z"]}}
```
yuki: those last two look like index drops and element-level shuffle. Could be quant decode instability + our array-serializer treating arrays as unordered during a merge step.
ben: check whether this is happening pre- or post- postprocess. If our NDJSON merge or prefix cache normalization turns arrays into sets for dedup, that could explain.
sam: traced: generator emits correct arrays, but our streaming concat + ndjson-merger sometimes collapses repeated array tokens when chunk boundary coincides with sub-token split; worst on int4. So regeneration is not the issue, it’s our merging heuristic.
rachel: mitigation options:
- strict: enforce `schema_guard: strict_array_order` at runtime and reject any response where array ordering differs from schema expectation
- soft-repair: `array_heal: pad_or_reorder` attempt one heuristic repair: if length matches but ordering changed, reorder using key-align heuristics (works if elements are unique IDs).
- opt-in per-route: enable repair only for low-risk ops like bulk_update where ids are integer keys and reordering is safe to fix by sorting.
yuki: telemetry additions: `funcall.parse_reason=missing_index|reorder|truncated_array|malformed_json` and `funcall.repaired_by=none|array_heal|ndjson_repair|fallback`. Also capture `array_hints` (e.g., elements_unique=true).
ben: test harness: run 300k synthetic cases with intentionally split array token boundaries. Evaluate false_repair (cases where repair changes semantics) and repair_precision (repair matches original). Thresholds: false_repair <0.01% and repair_precision >95%.
sam: I prototyped `array_heal` with rules: only apply if elements look like unique identifiers (ints/uuids) and original prompt implied ordered list. For bulk_update canary, this cut consumer failures 0.18% -> 0.02% in a 50k sample.
rachel: risks: reordering as a repair might hide generation bugs. So require telemetry flag `repaired=true` surfaced to customers in console and add a postmortem SLA trigger if repaired_ratio > 0.1% for 24h.
yuki: rollout plan:
1) canary routing: `schema_guard: strict_array_order` + `array_heal.opt_in:[bulk_update]`
2) enable telemetry for 72h and run 300k harness
3) owners: ben -> implement merger fix + array_heal, sam -> harness + canary config, rachel -> telemetry/dashboard.
deploy-bot: scheduled: harbor-int4 bulk_update array_heal canary on staging at 2026-04-01T05:00Z.
sam: I'll post a 12h parse_reason histogram and a sample set of repaired vs original arrays after the canary.
